subject: QAZ-v2 onboarding: dependency assessment and version lock request

Subject: QAZ-v2 onboarding: dependency assessment and version lock request

Hi team,

BrightRetail is ready to move QAZ-v2 into production on Hosted API next week. They asked us to guarantee the serving variant for 30 days while they validate end-to-end performance. They want a version lock (no model auto-roll to newer variants) and a short dependency/rollback plan documented.

I attached a first-pass compatibility matrix from the vendor and a rough rollback playbook. Can infra/dev confirm the following before I escalate to security/legal and the account team?

- Compatibility: does QAZ-v2 require any non-standard kernels or runtime flags that would block immediate deployment on our hosted pool?
- Resource profile: expected p99 latency and GPU memory for 4k context, and whether the runtime has any sequence-length regressions.
- Fallback: if we lock QAZ-v2 and it fails safety/regression checks, what is the fastest allowed rollback path (variant mapping to our current stable model)?
- Audit: what telemetry/logs will be retained for the 30-day lock window for legal review?

Please reply with concrete blockers and ETA for sign-off. I plan to request the version lock and exception by EOD Friday if we have no major blockers.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Soojin — thanks for the heads up. A couple of roadmap/PM questions before we lock: 

1) Business ask: is BrightRetail requesting a hard rollback window or a soft freeze with canary gating? We prefer canary gating with automatic fallback, but we can make a fixed 30-day lock if legal requires.
2) Metrics: what are the success criteria for the customer during the lock (latency SLO, token-quality checks, QA pass rate)? If we define these up front we can reduce churn.
3) Timeline: if infra gives a go, I need to notify sales/CS and schedule a short runbook review with the customer.

Recommend we: collect infra answers, draft the lock exception (include telemetry scope), and route to Security and Legal for sign-off. Happy to own the customer-facing communication.

Laura

TL;DR: likely OK but with two non-blocking caveats and one mitigation requirement.

Thanks for the packet, Soojin. I reviewed the vendor compatibility matrix and ran the model through our staging runner this morning. Notes: 

- Kernel/flags: QAZ-v2 uses a fused rotary + flash-attn kernel that our runtime supports, but only via the XLA-backed execution path on certain instance families. That path is available in Hosted but not yet in Dedicated pools.
- Memory/latency: baseline estimate for 4k context is ~10GB GPU memory and p95 latency ~120ms on A10x-class; p99 can spike to 260ms under high concurrency.
- Tokenizer edgecases: vendor uses a custom tokenizer that produces rare unknown tokens — we should add a short token normalization step to avoid OOV explosion in logs.

Caveats & required mitigation: 
1) Because the runtime selects XLA kernels for QAZ-v2, we must pin execution to a specific kernel variant (we can do that via model config) for the 30-day freeze; otherwise an automatic kernel upgrade could change performance unexpectedly.
2) We need a canary route (5% traffic) with the lock enforced for 48 hours before full traffic — that reduces rollback blast radius.

Rollback path: map QAZ-v2 -> QAZ-v1-compatible variant (qaz-v1-lite) which has identical API shape and lower memory footprint. Rollback steps in brief: drain new variant, switch routing to v1-lite, purge KV caches for the stickiness window, and run post-rollback smoke tests. The attached 'qaz-v2-rollback-playbook.md' has the steps and expected time (15-30 minutes).

ETA for infra confirmation: I can create the kernel-pin config and canary route by Friday EOD if legal doesn't require additional telemetry.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QAZ-v2 onboarding: dependency assessment and version lock request

Thanks Soojin and team — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- BrightRetail is comfortable with a 5% canary for 48 hours and then a full switch, as long as there is a documented rollback plan (your playbook is fine).
- Legal asked that telemetry retained during the 30-day lock include request/response timestamps, per-request model-id, and any safety flag hits. They do NOT want raw customer text retained longer than 7 days without explicit consent.
- We will sign the standard version-lock addendum if Redwood can confirm the kernel pin and that you will not auto-upgrade kernels during the lock window.

If you can send a one-page lock exception and the kernel pin config by EOD, we'll route to Legal for a final sign-off.

Regards,
James Holden
